title: A Wild Orangutan Treated His Own Wound With a Medicinal Plant

scenes.text: A wild orangutan was watched doctoring his own face.
June 2022, Sumatra. A big male called Rakus turns up with an open wound under his eye, probably from a fight with another male.
Then researchers watch him pick leaves from a climbing vine and chew them. He dabs the juice onto the wound with his finger, again and again.
Then he packs the chewed pulp over the top, like a bandage.
People across Southeast Asia use that same vine for pain and swelling. Tests show its chemicals fight bacteria.
Within five days the wound had closed, with no infection. No wild animal had ever been seen treating a wound with a medicine before.

description:
A wild orangutan was seen treating his own wound with a medicinal plant.
In June 2022 at the Suaq Balimbing research site in Sumatra's Gunung Leuser National Park, a male Sumatran orangutan named Rakus chewed leaves of the liana Akar Kuning (Fibraurea tinctoria), applied the juice to a wound on his face, and then covered it with the chewed leaves. The wound closed within five days without infection. The plant has antibacterial and anti-inflammatory compounds and is used in traditional medicine. Researchers from the Max Planck Institute of Animal Behavior reported it in Scientific Reports in May 2024 as the first documented case of its kind.
How do you think he knew which plant to use?
subject: orangutan
first_comment: Rakus wasn't born in that forest, so he may have learned the trick somewhere else. How do you think he worked it out?
